newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

National Australian triathlon coach Brett Sutton's elite training camp at Jindabyne has been hit by a chickenpox epidemic. Sixteen of Australia's top triathletes including world champions Jackie Gallagher and Greg Welch have been training together at the camp, and world junior champion Joanne King is now in doubt for the St George Grand Prix to be held in Adelaide this Sunday. Page 18.

Australian bowler Craig McDermott's hopes of surpassing Dennis Lillee's record as Australia's greatest wicket taker in Test cricket have been permanently ruined by a recent irreversible knee injury. As a result McDermott is expected today to announce his retirement from world class cricket. In a thirteen year career, he has taken 677 wickets in first-class matches. Page 20.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has supported the proposal to review the makeup of the Australian team midway through its South African cricket tour. The move is designed to adequately cater for the scheduled seven one-day games being planned afte the three test series. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Champion footballer Willie Carne's switch from the Brisbane Broncos rugby league team to the Queensland Reds rugby union team is a historic event in the history of the two rugby competitions in Australia. It indicates a reversal of the usual pattern of switching from the league to union codes. Page 49.

National Australian soccer coach Tony Venables has a rich selection of players to choose from for the next Socceroo squad. Many of Australia's seventy-five overseas-based players are hoping to be selected following an improvement in Australia's form this year when it won its first major trophy in twelve years against Norway, South Korea and New Zealand. Page 48.

Super League has suffered a blow with Channel Nine confirming that it will move its Monday night football coverage from the popular 8:30 pm timeslot to 9:30 pm instead. The decision was announced just two days before the launch of Super Leagues first offical competition in the country, the three day World Nines championship at Townsville. Page 48.
THE AGE

According to local commentators, Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor still deserves to head of the team despite having a poor batting record. They say he is an excellent captain with his record of thirteen wins, five losses, and four draws from twenty two Test series to prove it. Page B8.

Australian swimmer Michael Klim smashed the Australian 50 metres butterfly record and maintained his world No 2 ranking at the World Cup short course series in Glasgow. The win is a bright spot for the Australian squad, whose coach Gennadi Touretski is to be sentenced next week in a magistrate's court for refusing a breathalyser test. Page B6.

The Victorian Soccer Federation (VSF) is prepared to go FIDA in order to allow its Victorian Premier League to engage in direct competition with the national Ericsson Cup series. They are fighting for the right to run their competitions without interference from Soccer Australia. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Victorian batsman Matthew Elliott is expected to be included in the Australian cricket team set to tour South Africa this February. Elliott has been sidelined for eight weeks after a knee injury suffered when he collided with Mark Waugh in the Sydney Test. Page 88.

The Australian Davis Cup squad's practice session relocated to Melbourne after the session in Sydney was cancelled yesterday due to heavy rain. Australia will defend its title against France at White City on February 7-9. Page 86

Australian triple world motorbike champion Mike Doohan started the 1997 international competition in triumph yesterday when he went under the 500cc lap record in test races at Phillip Island yesterday. Riding a Honda he scored 2/100th of a second under te record set by Wayne Gardner in 1990. Page 83.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Despite confirming its place as the premier cricket team in the world by beating the West Indies in the Fourth Test, the Australian cricket team has been classed as the underdogs by the bookies in the forthcoming tour of South Africa. The bookkeepers cite that the home ground advantage will give South Africa the edge. Page 88.

The Australian swimming squad has performed well at the world short course series being held in Glasgow. Olympians Michael Klim and Matthew Dunn set national record performances in their opening events beating all competitors, while fifteen year old Natasha Brown, competing in her first world class event, won both the 200 m and 800m freestyle. Page 86.

The Australian rugby league team is determined to beat champions New Zealand at the upcoming World Nines championship series to be held in Townsville this weekend. New Zealand scored a shock win over Australia in the inaugural competition held in Figi last year. Page 78.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
